newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU exporters eye weekly 500,000 T grain exports.
newsitem.headline: EU exporters eye weekly 500,000 T grain exports.

text.p: The European Union needs to export something close to 500,000 tonnes of grain each week to meet a widely estimated target of 26 million tonnes by the end 1996/97 season, European grain exporters said on Friday.
It may not reach that target if sales are maintained at their current pace.
On Thursday the EU awarded 312,000 tonnes of grain, including 115,500 tonnes of wheat.
"The European Union is below 500,000 tonnes, so it may not make it (the target)," one exporter said.
EU grain and product export licences up to February 11 totalled 19.6 million tonnes, leaving some 6.4 million tonnes for possible export.
Product licences are measured in grain equivalent.
Exporters calculate the EU has at most 13 weeks left to export its grain on world markets, given that most importers stop buying old crop grain in May.
They said 26 million tonnes was a reasonable target for grain exports in view of record 1996 production in the EU and sustained world demand.
The target compares with a below-average 19.3 million tonnes of grain exported in 1995/96 at a time when stocks were tight and prices high.
Traders target EU soft wheat grain and processed products exports at 15 million tonnes in 1996/97 against 12.1 million in 1995/96.
That would include around 10 million tonnes of commercial soft wheat grain, with the rest in flour (grain equivalent).
They put exports of barley grain and processed products at 8.3 million tonnes against 4.5 million in 1995/96.
The EU is seen willing to track world markets while taking advantage of the lower subsidy costs implied by a strong dollar to sell grain abroad.
But it must balance this against remaining budget constraints and growing calls from U.S. farmers for a response to EU export subsidies, officials have said.
